content:
Three little pigs left home to build their own houses. The first built of straw, the second of sticks, and the third of strong bricks.
Along came a Wolf. He huffed and puffed and blew the straw house down, then the stick house too, and ate the first two pigs. But the brick house would not fall. The Wolf tried to climb down the chimney, and the clever third pig boiled a pot of water, so the Wolf jumped away and never returned.
So, little one, take your time to build things well, and you will be safe and snug. Close your eyes, and dream of a warm brick house.

A poor boy named Jack traded his cow for some magic beans. His mother was cross and threw them outside, but by morning a great beanstalk had grown up to the sky.
Jack climbed it and found a giant's castle. The giant roared, "Fee-fi-fo-fum!" but his wife hid Jack. Jack stole a bag of gold, then a hen that laid golden eggs, then a magic harp. As he climbed down, the giant followed, but Jack chopped the beanstalk, and the giant fell.
Jack and his mother lived happily, never poor again.
So, little one, a little courage and a kind heart can turn a small bean into a great adventure. Close your eyes now, and let the beanstalk of your dreams reach the stars.
